question: An older family album labels a trip “Queen Charlotte Islands,” but a current host writes “Haida Gwaii.” Am I necessarily looking at two different destinations?
generated_answer: - No, you are not necessarily looking at two different destinations. The Queen Charlotte Islands and Haida Gwaii refer to the same place. The name change reflects a shift towards recognizing and honoring the indigenous Haida people and their traditional name for the islands. The name “Haida Gwaii” means “Islands of the Haida People” in the Haida language. The name change was officially adopted by the Canadian government in 2010, but the term “Queen Charlotte Islands” may still be used in some contexts, especially in older documents or by people who are not familiar with the new name. However, both names refer to the same archipelago off the coast of British Columbia, Canada.
